subtype: Approach: studying with a friend and swapping questions [Action]
passage: After school in the small town, Hafsa and Shalini sat on the steps of the temple opposite the school gate, with their notebooks open. "Five questions each," said Hafsa. They wrote for ten minutes. Shalini wrote about the parts of a flower, and Hafsa wrote about seeds. Then they swapped papers. Hafsa answered fast. Shalini stopped at question four and said, "I don't remember the stigma." Hafsa explained it with a quick sketch, and Shalini nodded. When Shalini asked her about seeds, Hafsa found her own small gap, and they both laughed. They planned to swap again on Thursday.

qa.q: How many questions did each of them write?
qa.a: Each of them wrote five questions.

qa.q: What was Hafsa feeling when she found her own small gap and laughed?
qa.a: She felt amused and at ease. She could laugh because it was an ordinary slip and her friend was there to fill it.

qa.q: What alternative approach could the two girls use if they have less time, and why?
qa.a: They could each write just two questions on the parts they find hardest. Fewer questions aimed at gaps make a short session useful.

qa.q: How does Shalini see Hafsa's sketch of the stigma?
qa.a: Shalini sees a clear explanation that fills the gap, and nods. It helped that a classmate explained it in a way Shalini could see.

grounding: Two classmates each write five questions for the other on different parts of the chapter, and hearing each other's explanations fills small gaps.

subtype: Approach: studying with a friend and swapping questions [Action]
passage: After school on Tuesday, Rania and Emil sat at the kitchen table in Emil's flat in Copenhagen with their geography books open at volcanoes. "Five questions each," Rania said. "Then swap." They wrote in silence. Rania's questions were all about types of volcanoes. Emil's were all about why they erupt: the plates and the magma. They swapped and answered. Rania got stuck on Emil's question about plates sliding under each other. Emil explained it with two slices of bread pushed together on the table. Then Emil couldn't name a shield volcano, and Rania showed him the picture of the wide, flat one.

qa.q: What did Emil use to explain plates sliding under each other?
qa.a: Two slices of bread pushed together on the table.

qa.q: How might Rania have felt when the bread made the plates clear?
qa.a: She probably felt relieved and pleased that a gap she was stuck on suddenly made sense 😊

qa.q: What could make their next session even better?
qa.a: Swap topics, so each writes questions on the part they know less; mixing their questions is what showed the gaps.

qa.q: What was the session like for Emil?
qa.a: Emil got to teach with the bread and learn about shield volcanoes from Rania, so he gained as both teacher and learner.

grounding: Shows two classmates each writing five questions for the other on different parts of a chapter and filling small gaps by explaining.

subtype: Approach: studying with a friend and swapping questions [Action]
passage: The after-school study room was nearly empty when Lavanya and Vinita pushed two desks together. Their science test on electricity was on Thursday. Vinita tore a page in half. 'Five questions each, no peeking.' Lavanya wrote about circuits and switches; Vinita wrote about conductors and insulators. When they swapped, Lavanya groaned: she had forgotten why rubber covers wires. Vinita explained, tapping the fan's wire on the wall. Then Vinita couldn't draw a closed circuit, so Lavanya sketched one with a bulb and a cell, arrows showing the current. By the time the watchman jingled his keys, both pages were full of ticks.

qa.q: What was Lavanya feeling when she groaned at Vinita's question?
qa.a: She felt frustrated and a little embarrassed at forgetting why rubber covers wires.

qa.q: Which part of their method worked best, and why?
qa.a: Each writing questions on a different part of the chapter, because it exposed what the other had missed and let them explain it.

qa.q: How might Vinita see teaching Lavanya about rubber?
qa.a: Vinita gets to explain something she knows well, which likely leaves Vinita feeling confident before the test.

grounding: Illustrates two classmates swapping five questions each on different parts of a chapter and filling each other's gaps by explaining.
